state: Finite deterministic fixtures and test executions; no arbitrary programs or hidden production state.
cost: Bounded exhaustive fixture enumeration; the oracle scans each pattern at each boundary and compares the corresponding byte window. Test cost is intentionally independent of production claims.
forward: Run deterministic independent byte oracles, boundary cases, transformation laws and compatible-output fibers; assert exact values and explicit false-premise counterexamples. Passing finite checks does not establish universal correctness.

Oracle logic does not use production failure links. All fixtures are deterministic; comparisons include output order, offsets and multiplicity. Historical external mutation evidence is separate from the tests.
inverse: Exclude acceptance when an asserted production output differs from the independent oracle, a stated conditional law fails under its premises, or a compatible-output fiber differs from direct constraints. Unvisited inputs are outside this finite acceptance claim.

A passing observation admits every implementation agreeing on the tested fixture observations. Many implementations may differ elsewhere; test success cannot uniquely reconstruct source or establish universal correctness.
Direct byte-window equality supplies the independent specification; production failure-link machinery is not reused.
Tests exercise injective relabeling, ID permutation and prefix extension. A noninjective collision can create a match.
Removing inherited failure outputs must fail the empty/suffix-output boundary test; compilation success and assertion failure, not compilation error, establish this control.
checks: Debug/release twice; strict Clippy; rustfmt; source syntax twice; compiled mutant.
limitations: Partial syntax omits semantic resolution and macro expansion. Finite evidence is not proof. Allocation exhaustion untested; no executable approximation profile or downstream wiring claim.
